packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-18 - isolated first reading (unverified image reading)

No proposed identification of this record was in my context. I did nothing beyond the reader rules.

LAYOUT SURVEY (from overviews image-001 and image-008)
- Two faces of the same object: image-001 (face A) and image-008 (face B), each with tiles (002-007 for face A, 009-014 for face B, presumably a 3x2 grid of native-resolution tiles).
- The object is four separate narrow parchment strips laid side by side (approx 2.5-3.5 cm wide, 7.5-10.5 cm tall by the ruler), each a cut-down binding strip. Not a page; no full column, no margins or ruling visible at overview scale. A tight crop: column width and lines per column of the original cannot be determined.
- Face A: strip 1 (left, tallest) shows only very faint/abraded traces, plus a modern pencil number near its foot ("Fr. 15..."?). Strip 2 carries ~12-13 lines of a fairly large brown-ink script (one column fragment, text cut on both sides). Strip 3 carries ~8 visible lines, upper part rubbed. Strip 4 carries ~6 lines in its upper half, lower half rubbed/blank, plus a modern pencil mark.
- Face B: all four strips very faint/abraded; modern pencil numbers on strip 1 ("Fr. 151-4"?) and strip 2. Little or no legible ink at overview scale.
- No rubrics, coloured initials, glosses or running titles seen at overview scale. Orientation: the text on face A strips appears upright as photographed.

TILE image-002 (face A, upper left: strip 1 top and left edge of strip 2)
- Strip 1 (upper ~2/3): abraded, mottled surface; no ink strokes I can resolve as letters. [illegible / apparently text-less or fully rubbed]
- Strip 2, left edge only (beginnings of lines; full lines read on image-003):
  image-002 l1: ce Hur[...]
  image-002 l2: ?ingeri[...]
  image-002 l3: ?num ill[...]
  image-002 l4: m obser[...]
  image-002 l5: ?hamus[...]
  image-002 l6: ?tulo d[...]
  image-002 l7: ?inum ?[...]
  image-002 l8: dun[...]
  (these lines are repeated on image-003; not additional text)

TILE image-003 (face A, upper middle: strip 2 upper part, strip 3 upper part)
Crops made: rscratch/packet-18/s2_003.png, rscratch/packet-18/s3_003.png (greyscale, autocontrast, 2x).
Script: a single medium-large brown-ink hand, rounded, fairly upright, late cursive/humanistic-looking letter forms (round a, long s in "-sis", tall ascenders with slight hooks, d with leftward-curving ascender). Few abbreviation marks seen. Text cut on both left and right sides of each strip.

Strip 2 (left strip on this tile), lines from top of the strip:
  image-003 l1: [...]ce Hunga[...]
  image-003 l2: [...]?lengerum. ?[...]   (first letters very uncertain: could be "?ingerum", "?lengrum"; a dot/point after -um, then trace of a letter at the cut)
  image-003 l3: [...]uum illa q[...]   (or "illag[...]"; descender after a)
  image-003 l4: [...]m obseruai[...]  (or "obseruat[...]"; "obser" fairly clear)
  image-003 l5: [...]?thamus fu[...]  (or "su[...]"; first letters "?th" uncertain)
  image-003 l6: [...]?tulo dera[...]  (or "dere[...]"; d with looped back-curving ascender)
  image-003 l7: [...]?nunicatio[...]  (letters n/u/m minims ambiguous: "numicatio" or "nunicatio")
  image-003 l8: [...]duntax[...]

Strip 3 (right strip on this tile), from top:
  image-003 l1: [...]?h ?[...]  (faint, only an ascender letter readable)
  image-003 l2-l5: rubbed; at about l4 a band of BLUE-ish strokes ("?Hoc...", looks like later/different ink or pencil) - [illegible]
  image-003 l6: [...]?ceuensis Di[...]  (first 2 letters uncertain: "ce/ec"; "-ensis" clear with long s)
  image-003 l7: [...]?echtaus No[...]   (very uncertain; "-us No" clear, capital N)
  image-003 l8: [...]um prenor[...]   (or "prenom[...]"; cut at foot of tile)

TILE image-004 (face A, upper right: right edge of strip 3 (repeat of image-003, not new text) and strip 4 upper part)
Crop made: rscratch/packet-18/s4_004.png (greyscale, autocontrast, 2x).
Strip 3 right edge: repeats "...nsis Di[...]", "...us No[...]", "...?ranor/prenor[...]" already given on image-003; the rubbed upper area again shows faint blue-grey strokes - [illegible].

Strip 4, from top of strip (same brown-ink hand, more faded):
  image-004 l1: [...]?Consi?[...]   (or "conf/consi"; long-s or f after n uncertain; rest of line faint)
  image-004 l2: [...]?ne ?rat ?[...]  (very faint; "at" relatively clear)
  image-004 l3: [...]?ry ?[...] ?f[...]  (faint; tall descender letters)
  image-004 l4: [...]Com[...]   (C large/capital-like; rest of line rubbed)
  image-004 l5: [...]?nim cum m[...]  (or "nini/num"; "cum" probable; minims ambiguous)
  image-004 l6: modern pencil shelfmark-like note "?Fr. 151 ?" over the surface - not part of the text.
  Below: rubbed, [illegible].

TILE image-005 (face A, lower left: strip 1 lower part; left edge of strip 2 lower part)
- Strip 1 lower: no resolvable ink text; modern pencil note "Frag. 15?-4a" (or "151-4a") near the foot - modern label, not text.
- Strip 2 left edge (overlaps image-006, where full lines are read): "[...]tulo d[...]" / "?numica[...]" / "[...]? dunt[...]" / modern pencil "Frag. 151-3?" written across the strip / "[...]?e ?er[...]" / "?ucc[...] ma[...]" / "[...]m Aul[...]" / "?Dal?gemi[...]" / "?iac uel[...]". Read fully on image-006.

TILE image-006 (face A, lower middle: strip 2 lower part, strip 3 lower part)
Crops made: rscratch/packet-18/s2_006.png, rscratch/packet-18/s3_006.png (greyscale, autocontrast, 2x).
Overlap: top lines of this tile repeat image-003 l6-l8 of each strip; numbering below continues the strip's own line count from the top of the strip (strip line no. in brackets) so repeats are not double-counted.

Strip 2 (left):
  image-006 l1 [strip l6]: [...]?tulo dera[...]   (repeat of image-003 l6)
  image-006 l2 [strip l7]: [...]?numicatio[...]   (repeat of image-003 l7; final "o" clear)
  image-006 l3 [strip l8]: [...]?a duntaxa[...]   (repeat, now fuller: "duntaxa", end cut; a letter "a/e" before it)
     modern pencil "Frag. 151-3a" written between l8 and l9 - not text
  image-006 l4 [strip l9]: [...]?e ?eron[...]   (or "geron/zeron"; first letter faint)
  image-006 l5 [strip l10]: [...]?ucc[e]? nam d?[...]   (very uncertain: "?ucl nam d" / "suce..."; a tall ascender after d at the cut)
  image-006 l6 [strip l11]: [...]m Aula C[...]   (capital A; "Aula" fairly clear; capital C at cut)
  image-006 l7 [strip l12]: [...]Dal?gemis . ?[...]  (or "Dalgemi s."; g with large lower loop; point after; trace at cut)
  image-006 l8 [strip l13]: [...]?iac uel ?[...]   ("uel" probable; last line on strip, lower edge torn)

Strip 3 (right):
  image-006 l1 [strip l6]: [...]?ensis Di[...]   (repeat of image-003 l6, top of tile cut)
  image-006 l2 [strip l7]: [...]?Dechaus No[...]   (repeat; still very uncertain - letters before "us" could be "-ctius/-ctaus/-chius"; "No" with capital N, then ascender at cut)
  image-006 l3 [strip l8]: [...]um prenor[...]   (repeat; "pren-" fairly clear, then "o" and r/m at cut)
  image-006 l4 [strip l9]: [...]?ubre?fsius ?[...]  (very uncertain; long s/f clear mid-word, "-ius/-ius" then a letter at cut)
  image-006 l5 [strip l10]: [...]? ?[...]  (faint; [illegible], a dark blot mid-line)
  image-006 l6 [strip l11]: [illegible] (rubbed)
  image-006 l7 [strip l12]: [...]?Repohis?[...]  (very faint, near torn lower edge; [illegible] in substance)

TILE image-007 (face A, lower right: right edge of strip 3 lower part (repeat), strip 4 lower part)
- Strip 3 right edge repeats "...us No[...]", "...?ranor[...]", "...?ius ?[...]" - no new text; lower part rubbed, [illegible].
- Strip 4 lower: modern pencil "Frag. 151-1a" (or "151-2a"); below it the surface is rubbed with only faint grey traces, [illegible]. No further text lines resolvable.

TILE image-009 (face B, upper left: strip 1 upper, left edge of strip 2 upper)
- Strip 1: mottled, abraded surface; no ink letters resolvable. [illegible / no visible text]
- Strip 2 left edge: one small dark ink mark near the top ("?v" - a single letter or stroke); otherwise no text visible.

TILE image-010 (face B, upper middle: strip 2 upper, strip 3 upper)
Crop made: rscratch/packet-18/s3B_010_blue_eq.png (blue channel, equalized, 2x) - did not bring out letters.
- Strip 2: one dark ink mark "?v" near top left (same as on image-009); a dark stain at right edge mid-height; no text lines.
- Strip 3: a row of small holes across the upper part (the same row of holes is visible on face A strip 3, so these are through-holes, likely from sewing/binding); faint brownish traces at the top edge (?descenders of a cut line) and faint grey traces lower left ("?18"?), modern pencil "Frag. 151-2b" (or similar) mid-strip. No legible text. [illegible]

TILE image-011 (face B, upper right: right edge of strip 3 upper (repeat), strip 4 upper)
- Strip 3 right edge: as on image-010, no legible text.
- Strip 4: abraded; faint dark specks in the upper third (a few isolated strokes, possibly remains of letters, e.g. one tall stroke at right) but no letter sequence resolvable. [illegible]

TILE image-012 (face B, lower left: strip 1 lower, left edge of strip 2 lower)
- Strip 1: modern pencil "Frag. 151-4v"; no ink text visible. [no visible text]
- Strip 2 left edge: modern pencil "Frag. 15?[...]"; a few scattered dark specks/strokes lower down ("?ag ?" - not resolvable as words); torn lower edge. [illegible]

TILE image-013 (face B, lower middle: strip 2 lower, strip 3 lower)
- Strip 2: modern pencil "Frag. 151-3v"; below it scattered faint brown specks ("?g ?", a possible letter fragment) - no resolvable text. [illegible]
- Strip 3: faint horizontal grey bands that may be abraded lines of writing, no letters resolvable at native resolution. [illegible]

TILE image-014 (face B, lower right: strip 3 right edge lower, strip 4 lower)
- Strip 3: abraded, faint grey traces only. [illegible]
- Strip 4: modern pencil "Frag. 151-?" with a correction/overwriting ("-1v"/"-2v"?); no ink text visible. [illegible]

SUMMARY / LIMITATIONS
- Areas read: face A strips 2, 3 and 4 (all visible lines). Face A strip 1 and all of face B show no resolvable ink text (abraded or blank); contrast/channel crops did not help on face B.
- Modern pencil labels (not part of the text): face A strips 1/2/4 "Frag. 151-4a", "151-3a", "151-1a"(?); face B strips 1/2/4 "151-4v", "151-3v", "151-?v". These suggest the strips are numbered pieces 1-4 with a/v (recto/verso?) faces; read as modern labels only.
- Best continuous text (face A strip 2, 13 lines, both edges cut, so only 1-3 words per line):
    [...]ce Hunga[...] / [...]?lengerum. ?[...] / [...]uum illa q[...] / [...]m obseruai[...] / [...]?thamus fu[...] / [...]?tulo dera[...] / [...]?numicatio[...] / [...]?a duntaxa[...] / [...]?e ?eron[...] / [...]?ucc? nam d?[...] / [...]m Aula C[...] / [...]Dal?gemis . ?[...] / [...]?iac uel ?[...]
  Face A strip 3: [...]?ceuensis Di[...] / [...]?echtaus No[...] / [...]um prenor[...] / [...]?ubre?fsius ?[...]
  Face A strip 4: [...]?Consi?[...] / [...]?ne ?rat[...] / [...]Com[...] / [...]?nim cum m[...]
- The strips are too narrow to establish column width or lines per column; I cannot tell whether strips 2-4 are from the same column or how they align with one another. Script appears to be one hand throughout face A (brown ink, rounded cursive with long s); faint blue/grey strokes in strip 3's rubbed upper area are of uncertain nature.
- Suggested further imaging: UV/multispectral of face B and of face A strip 1 and the upper half of strip 3, where text is presumably present but abraded.
- I did not stop on the image limit. All 14 images viewed once; 6 crops made in rscratch/packet-18/.
